subject: Cross-border escrow & subprocessor-chain decomposition — questions and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@zentechhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-border escrow & subprocessor-chain decomposition — initial ask

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As part of our DPA and UK Addendum review, Legal at ZenTech asked for a clear decomposition of how data would traverse international boundaries and which subprocessors touch tokens or unredacted payloads. Specifically they're asking:

- A table listing each subprocessor's role, processing location(s), and whether they receive logs, cached prefixes, or persistent copies.
- Which subprocessors would be covered by an escrow/backup in the EU under the proposed contractual flow.
- Any choke points where data is transformed (e.g., pseudonymization, tokenization) and the responsible party.

Can you share a mapping and a short gap list by EOD so we can update our DPA redlines? We know this touches the UK IDTA questions and the TIA scoping.

Appreciate it — if easier, we can take a 30-min call with Laura and Kim.

Cheers,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Privacy, ZenTech Health

Attachments: zen_request_summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@zentechhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border escrow & subprocessor-chain decomposition — initial ask

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a decomposition and attached a CSV that maps subprocessors to artifact types and regions. High level summary below; full details in redwood_subprocessor_chain.csv attached.

- Primary flow: Customer -> Redwood API (hosted in eu-west-1 for ZenTech) -> Serving runtime (GPU pools in eu-west-1) -> Optional caching layer (prefix cache in s3-eu) -> Analytics partner (metrics ingest, no raw payload retained) -> Backup/escrow (encrypted snapshots stored in EU escrow provider).

- Subprocessors that receive anything resembling raw payload:
  1) Redwood infra (owned) — processing in eu-west-1 — does full inference, holds KV cache briefly (ephemeral), not retained beyond session unless customer opts-in.
  2) Escrow provider (EscrowEU Ltd) — stores encrypted backups; holds ciphertext only; key custodian is Redwood KMS in customer region.
  3) Model telemetry partner (InsightOps) — receives telemetry/hashed prompts for quality monitoring; we can provide pseudonymized sets on request.

- Transform points: pseudonymization happens in the preprocessing microservice (owned by Redwood) before analytics handoff; key rotation and HSM-backed KMS handled by Kimberly's team.

Gap list for DPA/UK Addendum / TIA:
- Need explicit DocuSign addendum that assigns EscrowEU Ltd as subprocessors under the UK Addendum language.
- Confirm whether ZenTech requires escrowed data to be accessible only under court order vs. Redwood admin access.
- Verify if InsightOps needs additional pseudonymization tooling (we can provide deterministic salts for linkage tests).

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_chain.csv (csv), escrow_flow_diagram.svg (svg)

Proposed next steps:
- Laura: draft a short DPA clause for escrow and subprocessors we can share.
- Kim: confirm KMS HSM attestation dates and whether we can provide a signed statement.
- Sofia/Evan: pick 30-min slot next week if you'd prefer a sync.

—Connor
Product Lead, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Li <evan.li@zentechhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@zentechhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2027 13:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border escrow & subprocessor-chain decomposition — initial ask

Connor,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — the CSV is very helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from Legal/InfoSec:

1) For the escrow provider, will Redwood retain the encryption keys, or will ZenTech hold them via a split-key arrangement? Our counsel prefers customer-held keys where possible for EU residency assurances.
2) For the caching layer in s3-eu, what is the retention SLA by default and can it be reduced to 0 days for regulated customers?
3) If InsightOps only receives hashed prompts, please confirm the hash algorithm and whether salts are shared.

Also, will adding EscrowEU Ltd to the UK Addendum require a separate TIA update? If so, can you surface the ticket/DocuSign flow so we can track approval internally.

Evan
Senior Counsel, ZenTech Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@zentechhealth.com>, Evan Li <evan.li@zentechhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border escrow & subprocessor-chain decomposition — initial ask

Hi Sofia/Evan —

Quick answers and action owners below:

1) Escrow keys: Redwood proposes a split-holder model: EscrowEU holds ciphertext; ZenTech may elect customer-managed KMS to hold key shares. We'll offer both options and document in the addendum. (Owner: Kimberly)
2) Cache retention: default is 24 hours for prefix cache; we can offer 0-day retention for regulated SKUs via a configuration flag (Owner: Connor/Infra).
3) InsightOps hashing: SHA-256 with per-customer salt; salt is not shared by default. We can provide an HMAC-based flow if you need deterministic linkage without salt exposure (Owner: InsightOps PO; we'll coordinate).

DocuSign/TIA flow: we'll generate a proposed addendum and route via our legal e-sign workflow. I'll create a DocuSign envelope and share the link — Connor will include the ticket id in the reply.

Next steps we will take today:
- Kimberly: produce KMS/HSM attestation and confirm timeline.
- Connor: push updated CSV (flags column for retention options) and draft the DPA addendum language.
- Laura: create DocuSign envelope and pre-fill parties; expect link in the next 48 hours.

If you'd like a short technical ramp call, Connor/Kimberly and I are available Tues/Wed morning next week PST.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_docsign_tia_addendum.docx (docx)
